modelNote: No -m flag was passed on any of these three runs; the fresh CODEX_HOME had no config.toml so the CLI fell back to its built-in default model. runs.purpose: Test whether a per-invocation -c skills.config override suppresses a specific skill's listing without touching config.toml on disk.
Repeat to confirm determinism of the suppression result (2/2, byte-identical input_tokens both times).

cliOverridesReachSkillsConfigPerSession.evidence: 2/2 runs: `-c 'skills.config=[{path="...",enabled=false}]'` removed exactly the targeted skill (test-echo-skill) from the listing while leaving all 66 other skills present; the fresh CODEX_HOME never gained a config.toml (verified by listing the dir after both runs), so the override is genuinely session-scoped and non-persisting.
cliOverridesReachSkillsConfigPerSession.classificationImpact: This is the finding that can move compileCodex's execSupport away from 'recipe' — codex has a real, verified per-session suppression route via -c skills.config, no launcher/recipe file-juggling required. (Classification change itself is out of scope here — skill-heaven is being edited by another agent — this is the evidence, not the edit.)

tokenIntrospectionOnCompletedTurn.evidence: All three runs produced a `turn.completed` event carrying a full usage object: input_tokens, cached_input_tokens, cache_write_input_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_output_tokens. This directly answers the previously-quota-blocked cell: `codex exec --json` DOES emit per-run token counts on a completed turn.

authPropagationStillHolds.verdict: YES — unchanged from the original G1 result
authPropagationStillHolds.evidence: All three runs authenticated successfully via the auth.json copy into a fresh $CODEX_HOME; no 'not logged in' or usage-limit error was observed this time (2026-07-25 quota window has passed, as the founder indicated).
